hints: Remember an oxidising agent gets reduced itself while it oxidises the other species, so look for which species gains electrons in each equation.
In the first reaction $\text{Br}_2$ changes to $\text{HBr}$, so $\text{Br}_2$ is the oxidiser and $\text{SO}_2$ is the species oxidised.
In the second reaction $\text{Cl}_2$ oxidises bromide to $\text{Br}_2$, so link the two results to order all three from strongest to weakest oxidiser.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes an oxidising agent**

An oxidising agent oxidises another species and is itself reduced. Reduction means gain of electrons or fall in oxidation number. So in each equation, find the species whose oxidation number falls.

Rule to use:
$$\text{oxidising agent is reduced, reducing agent is oxidised}$$

**Analyse reaction 1**

Look at $\text{Br}_2\text{(aq)} + \text{SO}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow 2\text{HBr(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(aq)}$.

Bromine goes from $0$ in $\text{Br}_2$ to $-1$ in $\text{HBr}$, so it is reduced. Sulfur goes from $+4$ in $\text{SO}_2$ to $+6$ in $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, so it is oxidised. This tells us $\text{Br}_2$ acts as the oxidising agent and can oxidise $\text{SO}_2$. Therefore $\text{Br}_2$ is a stronger oxidising agent than $\text{SO}_2$.

**Analyse reaction 2**

Look at $2\text{HBr(aq)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{Br}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{HCl(aq)}$.

Chlorine goes from $0$ in $\text{Cl}_2$ to $-1$ in $\text{HCl}$, so it is reduced. Bromine goes from $-1$ in $\text{HBr}$ to $0$ in $\text{Br}_2$, so it is oxidised. This tells us $\text{Cl}_2$ acts as the oxidising agent and can oxidise bromide to bromine. Therefore $\text{Cl}_2$ is a stronger oxidising agent than $\text{Br}_2$.

**Put the order together**

From Step 2: $\text{Br}_2 > \text{SO}_2$. From Step 3: $\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2$. Combining gives:
$$\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{SO}_2$$
So $\text{Cl}_2$ is the strongest oxidising agent and $\text{SO}_2$, which actually acts as a reducing agent here, is the weakest oxidising agent.

options.A: Incorrect. This puts $\text{Br}_2$ strongest and $\text{Cl}_2$ weakest, which is backwards. Reaction 2 shows $\text{Cl}_2$ oxidises $\text{Br}^-$ to $\text{Br}_2$, so $\text{Cl}_2$ must be stronger than $\text{Br}_2$, not weaker.
options.B: Correct and well done. $\text{Cl}_2$ oxidises $\text{Br}^-$ to $\text{Br}_2$, and $\text{Br}_2$ oxidises $\text{SO}_2$ to sulfate, giving the order strongest to weakest as $\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{SO}_2$.
options.C: Incorrect. While $\text{Cl}_2$ is correctly strongest, $\text{SO}_2$ is placed above $\text{Br}_2$. Reaction 1 shows $\text{Br}_2$ oxidises $\text{SO}_2$, so $\text{Br}_2$ must be the stronger oxidiser of the two.
options.D: Incorrect. This makes $\text{SO}_2$ the strongest oxidiser. In fact $\text{SO}_2$ is oxidised by $\text{Br}_2$ in reaction 1, so it is acting as a reducing agent and is the weakest oxidising agent of the three.
